Q: SSHException: OpenSSH private key file checkints do not match A:

the error appears to refer to a password string that does not match the password needed to decrypt the id_rsa (private key)

if I make sure that the password (second parameter) of this function paramiko.RSAKey.from_private_key_file(id_rsa_path, passcode) matches exactly the password used for the private key, no error is produced.

Since I was reading the password from a text file, I needed to be very careful ensuring that the line read had only the characters that make up the password, (no extra non-visible characters), so If I using strip() on that line string will take care of new line carachters and empty spaces and using a function like re.sub('\W_','') to substitute any non-alphanumerica caracters on the string should ensure the password read from the file matches the one I used for the private key when it was generated (assuing that only alphanumeric characters were used.

Q: Using advisory locks to coordinate database activity A:

With NullPool there is no pool — "returning" the connection closes the socket, and Postgres drops every session-level advisory lock on that backend.

Q: Tomcat webapps folder is ruined when putting a new WAR file A:

#Sounds like "antiResourceLocking" Disclaimer: 1. Yes, I know this is an old question. 2. Completely untested.

I have not tried this, so this is untested purely "by the books" stuff. Here goes.

The Tomcat7 documentation at least mentions that you need extra steps for hot deploy on Windows. Namely...

on Windows, this assumes that anti-locking features (see Context configuration) are enabled, otherwise it is not possible to delete the resources of a running web application.

...and the appropriate configuration switch seems to be something called antiResourceLocking, which apparently...

allows full webapp hot deploy and undeploy on platforms or configurations where file locking can occur

(Source here.)

And I'm not sure, but all of this does indeed sound a bit like "undefined behavior can happen if you try to hot-deploy on Windows WITHOUT antiResourceLocking=true". And that sounds just terrible.

##Further reading

  • Matrix. Judging by the matrix in the documentation, I think it's quite complicated.
    (So my personal bottom line here is: I will just NOT use automatic-deployment, unless I absolutely have to. And rather do what you did and manually delete DIRs and unpack WARs.)
